title: Dry run: linear scans inside binary search, 6 copies of 4

steps.note: Setup: start = 0, end = 10, ans = [-1,-1]. The target 4 sits at indices 2 to 7 (six copies).
mid is the centre of the range.
A match, so we enter the match branch.
The left neighbour is also 4, so we take the left-scan branch. The right-scan branch (else-if) is skipped entirely.
nums[4] is 4, so we enter the while body.
We only get here while nums[j] == target, so nums[j] != target is always false. The line 18 assignment to ans[0] can never run.
Step left. The inner if is false again for j = 3 and j = 2 (both are 4s).
j = 2, still a 4, the first one. The inner if is false again.
nums[1] = 2, so the while loop exits. We left the run of 4s without ever setting ans[0]. Index 2 was the answer. The scan was also O(n), not O(log n), for long runs.
ans[1] = mid = 5. But the last 4 is at index 7, and ans[0] is still -1.
The match branch never changes start or end, so they are still 0 and 10.
It matches again, repeats the same scan and ends in the same state. This repeats forever, giving Time Limit Exceeded. Final answer would have been [-1,5] instead of [2,7].
